claim: Agent Skills open standard spec: folder structure, frontmatter fields, progressive disclosure loading model, validation tooling
quote: A skill is a directory containing, at minimum, a SKILL.md file... Agents load skills progressively, pulling in more detail only as a task calls for it.

claim: MCP specification 2025-11-25: three primitives (tools, resources, prompts), JSON-RPC base protocol, security and trust principles
quote: Resources: Context and data, for the user or the AI model to use. Prompts: Templated messages and workflows for users. Tools: Functions for the AI model to execute.

claim: MCP ecosystem has grown to 10,000+ tracked servers as of mid-2026; OAuth 2.1 + PKCE S256 mandated for remote servers
quote: Spec 2025-11-25 mandates OAuth 2.1 with PKCE S256, RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata, and RFC 8707 Resource Indicators.

claim: Claude Code plugin system: directory structure, plugin.json schema, marketplace distribution, background monitors, --plugin-dir flag
quote: Common mistake: Don't put commands/, agents/, skills/, or hooks/ inside the .claude-plugin/ directory. Only plugin.json goes inside .claude-plugin/.

claim: Claude Code skills documentation: all frontmatter fields, invocation matrix, dynamic context injection, subagent forking, scoping rules
quote: disable-model-invocation: true — Only you can invoke the skill. Use this for workflows with side effects or that you want to control timing.

claim: Design heuristic for MCP primitives: Tools for action, Resources for context, Prompts for interaction patterns; naming and URI conventions
quote: Tools are action enablers... Resources represent structured data elements... Prompts are predefined templates, instructions, or interface-integrated commands.

claim: Resources and Prompts are the most-skipped MCP primitives, leading to overuse of tool calls for context retrieval
quote: MCP Prompts and Resources: The Primitives You're Not Using — most servers focus entirely on tools and miss significant expressiveness.

claim: MCP TypeScript SDK (⭐ 12.6k) and Python SDK (⭐ 23.2k): code examples for defining tools with Zod and FastMCP decorator API
quote: The MCP TypeScript SDK is the Tier 1 official SDK, the most feature-complete, best-supported implementation available.

claim: Tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are hints not guarantees; defaults are deliberately cautious
quote: Annotations are not guarantees. This distinction shapes everything about how they should be used.

claim: Claude Code uses readOnlyHint to enable concurrent dispatch; clients show confirmation dialogs for destructiveHint tools
quote: Claude Code uses readOnlyHint to determine parallelism — tools marked read-only execute concurrently at roughly double the dispatch rate.

claim: Tool poisoning (rug pull) attack: attackers embed malicious instructions in tool descriptions or change them post-approval
quote: Tool Poisoning is a vulnerability where an attacker embeds malicious instructions within the descriptions of MCP tools... a user that previously approved a tool may end up with a tool that changed since their approval happened.

claim: Single-purpose server pattern: one server per domain reduces blast radius on tool compromise
quote: Each MCP server should have one clear, well-defined purpose. Layer security controls throughout your architecture rather than implementing a monolithic approach.

claim: MCP cheat sheet: stateless servers behind load balancers, listChanged notifications, MCP Inspector for debugging
quote: A remote MCP server can now run behind a plain round-robin load balancer and let clients cache tools/list responses... Use the MCP Inspector tool to debug and validate your server interactively.

claim: MCP security spec: confused deputy, token passthrough prohibition, scope minimization, SSRF mitigation, session hijacking
quote: MCP servers MUST NOT accept any tokens that were not explicitly issued for the MCP server. Token passthrough is explicitly forbidden.

claim: Indirect prompt injection: tool responses containing document bodies or scraped pages can carry malicious instructions into LLM context
quote: Tool responses are attacker-controllable input — any document body, scraped page, webhook payload, error message, or search result that the agent will read with the same attentiveness it gives a user message deserves the same scrutiny.

claim: CSA agentic MCP security guide: audit logging, rate limiting, kill switches, sandboxing
quote: Use OAuth 2.1, scope tokens per tool, validate inputs with Zod or Pydantic, sanitize outputs, rate limit, sandbox with Docker or microVMs, audit-log every call.

claim: Over-broad scope is the common failure mode across all MCP server implementations
quote: Prevention requires multiple security layers: Input validation, least-privilege permissions, tool registry governance, and continuous monitoring. No single control is sufficient.

claim: Community resource repo for MCP client development guides and reference implementations
quote: model-context-protocol-resources: guides, client development guide, reference implementations for MCP.
